one_liner:
A goalkeeper-defense game where the player uses The player is the sole defender (the goalkeeper) in a single 3D pitch/arena and never takes a shot themselves; one computer-controlled attacker occupies the shooting spot at a time and fires at the goal from varying angles, distances and speeds in the "battle royale" sense the brief names - escalating, survival pressure rather than a literal crowd of simultaneous scoring attackers - and the player moves, dives and blocks to deny every shot. The win condition is inverted from a normal soccer game: the human's goal is to concede nothing, not to score.
.
why_this_opportunity:
Goalkeeper Royale offers Being the last line of defense against an unrelenting computer-driven onslaught - survival pressure borrowed from battle royale ("everyone else is eliminated, only you are left standing"), re-aimed at a goalkeeper who has to outlast the AI's attack rather than outscore it. The brief's "battle royale" word is read as that survival-pressure framing taken from its own text, not as a request for multiplayer play.
. The opportunity rests on claim-07555f3148 and cites claim-008c6635b7, claim-07555f3148, claim-0b9f911511, claim-2a9ae48a74, claim-37418f4224, claim-5ce8a2013e, claim-5f2a90b55e, claim-7d4de2db07, claim-86bdd693be, claim-8788cb4757, claim-9c0387d80e, claim-c56352d968, claim-ce911ba6ad, claim-cf8d78cc8d, claim-d43b8fd7f2, claim-ea12f1f964, claim-f4a5134985. Poki is primary (audience regions br, de, fr, gb, id, us; supports rewarded placements).

audience.player_description: A casual player on a desktop browser who wants to be playing within seconds, in sessions of about 2 minutes.

monetization.rationale: Short, round-based arcade sessions with a natural end-of-round break fit a rewarded continue/extra-life offer, with interstitials placed between rounds rather than mid-save - the same placement pattern observed on CrazyGames' existing goalkeeper and penalty-genre titles (see snap-crazygames-goalkeeper-wiz, snap-crazygames-penalty-listing).

mvp: Core loop: A round starts -> the AI attacker takes shots in escalating speed/angle variety and shrinking windup time -> the player reads the windup and dives/moves/blocks -> a save extends the player's defensive streak and raises the next shot's difficulty; a concede costs a life -> the round ends when the player has survived the set number of shots (win) or runs out of lives (loss) -> streak and save-accuracy are tallied, then the player retries or advances to a harder round via the same tuned shot set, not new content.

A single tap control: The player is the sole defender (the goalkeeper) in a single 3D pitch/arena and never takes a shot themselves; one computer-controlled attacker occupies the shooting spot at a time and fires at the goal from varying angles, distances and speeds in the "battle royale" sense the brief names - escalating, survival pressure rather than a literal crowd of simultaneous scoring attackers - and the player moves, dives and blocks to deny every shot. The win condition is inverted from a normal soccer game: the human's goal is to concede nothing, not to score.
One content set with a data-driven difficulty ramp
Score and personal best, persisted locally
A rewarded placement at a natural moment in the loop (continue or bonus), never forced
Interstitials between sessions only, never inside one
Poki SDK: init, loading-progress, gameplay-start-stop, rewarded, interstitial, pause-audio-during-ads
out_of_scope: Multiplayer and any online play — networking multiplies the test surface and needs a server nobody has budgeted
Metagame layers: daily quests, battle pass, login rewards — retention systems are validated after the core loop is, not before
Character or skin customization and a cosmetics shop
Story, cutscenes and dialogue — text multiplies localization cost
A second mode or content set — one proves the loop; more is content, not validation
An IAP economy or premium currency
Platforms beyond the set: y8, gamedistribution — platform sprawl multiplies compliance work
prototype_must_prove: A first-time player understands the tap control without instruction
The core loop produces an unforced desire to retry within one 120-second session
The rewarded placement reads as a favour rather than an interruption

success_criteria.label: D1 retention
success_criteria.rationale: Below this a short-session title without a metagame has no path to sustained portal traffic.

success_criteria.label: Median session near target
success_criteria.rationale: Shorter than this and the placements the monetization model counts on never get a chance to show.

kill_criteria.label: First-time players do not understand the control
kill_criteria.rationale: The title is scoped around one control scheme and no tutorial. If that scheme needs teaching, the scope assumption is wrong.

kill_criteria.label: Players do not retry unprompted
kill_criteria.rationale: Replay is the retention system here, in place of content. Without immediate retry there is neither retention nor an ad moment.

kill_criteria.label: The prototype consumed most of the timebox
kill_criteria.rationale: A prototype that needs more than 60% of the timebox is evidence the scope does not fit it, and production would overrun by more.

Replay comes from a system (score chase), not from more content
Asset budget capped at 120 unique assets (high asset complexity)
